definitions.explanation: A distinguishing feature or object used as a reference point to identify a location or thing. Used both for physical markers and visual cues for navigation.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}い{屋根|やね}が{目印|めじるし}です。
examples.english: The red roof is the landmark.

examples.japanese: {荷物|にもつ}にリボンを{付|つ}けて{目印|めじるし}にした。
examples.english: I tied a ribbon on my luggage as a mark to identify it.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}の{大|おお}きな{時計台|とけいだい}を{目印|めじるし}にして{歩|ある}いてきてください。
examples.english: Please walk toward the big clock tower in front of the station as your landmark.

notes:
USAGE:
{目印|めじるし} is used when giving directions ("look for X as a landmark") or when marking something for later identification. It is a very common everyday word.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {目印|めじるし}にする (to use as a landmark/marker)
- {目印|めじるし}になる (to serve as a landmark)
- {目印|めじるし}を{付|つ}ける (to put a mark on something)
- いい{目印|めじるし} (a good landmark)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{目標|もくひょう} means "goal" or "target," not a visual marker. {標識|ひょうしき} refers to an official sign (like a road sign), while {目印|めじるし} is any distinguishing feature used as a reference point.
